. In this surah, the very first verse already contains a definite indication, and this indication creates a specific picture regarding cosmic events, explaining what role the believers play in these events, what role the Prophet ﷺ plays, and what the limits of the sphere of action of the believers and of the Prophet are in human life and in these cosmic occurrences and events. This indication lies in the phrase:

﴿Idha ja'a ... wal-fath﴾ (1:110) "When the help of Allah comes, and the victory." All depends upon Allah's help, and Allah's time is fixed; the form in which help will come is also determined, and the purpose for which this help will be given is also fixed. The Prophet and his companions have no authority regarding its arrival, nor do they have any role in Divine help. Nor does their personal effort have any part in that help. Nor do their selves have any share in it. This help is an event which, according to Allah's decision, does not come from their persons but from outside. For them it is sufficient honour that Allah apparently brings this help through them, appoints them as its guardians, and they become trustees of this help and victory. Thus their share in victory and triumph is only this: that people enter the religion of Islam in multitudes, both they and others.

In the light of this indication and the thought arising from it, regarding this honour and dignity which came about through their hands in the manifestation of help and victory, the status of the Messenger of Allah and his companions is determined. Their rank and station now is that they turn towards Allah and become completely thankful. They praise and glorify Allah and seek forgiveness for their shortcomings. This praise and gratitude is for the fact that Allah made them the trustees and custodians of the Islamic revolution, and by granting help to His religion and making it dominant, He bestowed a favour upon all of humanity. The Messenger of Allah became victorious, and people entered the religion in multitudes, "in this great news," although before this they were blind, misguided, and in severe loss.

Why seek forgiveness? It is for the psychological factors which enter hearts in a very subtle manner and settle there. When a force comes to power after a long and tireless struggle, a kind of pride secretly enters its psychology in the intoxication of triumph and success; then after hardships and sacrifices, some shortcomings also occur in a person through joys. These hidden psychological viruses can only be protected against through repentance and seeking forgiveness; therefore, the command to seek forgiveness is given here.

This seeking of forgiveness is also because, during the long period of struggle, due to tireless circumstances and severe difficulties and very distressing conditions, a suffocation comes into the human heart. A person thinks that the arrival of Allah's help has been delayed, and the caller is shaken. As has been said in al-Baqarah (2:214):

﴿Am hasibtum ... inna nasrallahi qarib﴾ (2:214) "Did you think that you would enter Paradise while the situations that came upon those who came before you have not yet come upon you? They were afflicted with poverty and hardship and were shaken, until the Messenger and those who believed with him cried out: When will the help of Allah come? Listen! The help of Allah is near."

Therefore, the command was given to seek forgiveness.

The command to seek forgiveness is also given because a person falls short in praising Allah. Thus, however much a person's striving may be, it is limited, and a person is weak. And Allah's blessings are always countless and His bounty is general.

﴿Wa in ta'uddu ... tuhsuha﴾ (14:34) "If you were to count the favours of Allah, you could not enumerate them." Therefore, for this shortcoming, the command to seek forgiveness is given.

At the occasion of victory and triumph, there is also a subtle point in glorification and seeking forgiveness: that at the place of pride and boasting, a consciousness is created within the self that a human being is always at the level of helplessness and shortcoming. Therefore he should come down a little from the level of the great, and ask his Lord for forgiveness of his shortcomings. In this way, tendencies toward pride and boasting are eliminated from human consciousness and human psychology.

If the consciousness settles in the heart of a victor that he is a figure of helplessness and shortcoming, and that he should seek forgiveness from Allah for his shortcomings, then such a victor can never commit oppression and transgression against the defeated people. Such a person thinks that it is Allah's Being whose help has made him sovereign over these people. Had Allah's help not been there, he would be a humble servant of little worth; and the authority Allah gave him, He gave so that Allah may desire some good and welfare for the defeated people. In truth, victory is attained through Allah's help. The help is also His, and the victory is also His, and this is not the victory of the conqueror but the victory of Allah's religion. And the outcome of all affairs lies in Allah's hand, and all decisions return to Allah.

This is the manner and the lofty horizon upon which the Qur'an invites all of humanity to fix their gaze, so that they may rise step by step to that lofty horizon, which is the supreme level of nobility and goodness. Upon reaching it, a person becomes great, because he withdraws from his own greatness. Here his soul becomes free and attains joy, because it adopts servitude to Allah.

In short, this is a freedom in which a person is liberated from personal and material bonds, and a person becomes one of the spiritual creatures of Allah, and reaches a station where Allah's pleasure becomes his pleasure. After attaining this station, he becomes a mujahid, and the direction of his striving is to support goodness in the form of an Islamic order and to make truth into reality; and then, after the establishment of the Islamic order, he should bring such development to this earth and provide such leadership to the world that the world becomes free of evil and corruption. This leadership should be righteous, pure and constructive, and its aim should be to spread and develop every goodness, and thus turn the direction of all affairs toward Allah.

If a person is a frog in the limited well of his own self and is confined in it, then his efforts for freedom become futile. After freedom he becomes a slave of his desires; he is caught in lusts and appetites. If a person is not freed from the low circle of carnal desires, then other freedoms are futile. Islam wants that, along with other freedoms, a person be freed from carnal desires too, so that he remembers Allah and becomes His servant.

These are the manners of prophethood, which have remained inseparable from prophethood, and Allah's will is that humanity rise up to the horizons of these prophetic manners. And if they cannot reach there, their gaze should at least be upon that horizon. See, Yusuf (peace be upon him) is seen to have reached this station. The treasures of power of Egypt have come into his hands. His dream has come true. When he raised his parents upon his throne, his brothers prostrated before him, and Yusuf (peace be upon him) said to his parents: Father! This is the interpretation of my dream; Allah has made it a reality. See Allah's favour, that He brought me out of prison, and brought you all from the desert to Egypt, although Satan had sown discord between my brothers and me. Surely my Lord is subtle in His arrangements; indeed He is the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.

In short, on such an occasion, Yusuf (peace be upon him) comes out of the atmosphere of height, honour, joy and delight, and occupies himself in remembrance and reflection, praising his Lord. He is at the peak of power, all his dreams have become reality, but his invocation is this:

﴿Rabbi qad ataytani ... bil-salihin﴾ (12:101) "My Lord! You have given me sovereignty and taught me the interpretation of matters. Creator of the heavens and the earth, You are my Protector in this world and the Hereafter. Let me die as a Muslim and join me with the righteous."

Here, authority and power fade into the background. This gathering of family, brothers and sisters, and the joy of meeting relatives and parents after a long period, fades away. Now in this final scene we see an individual who is pleading before the Lord, and his request is that his Islam be preserved and that his society be with the righteous. And this rank can be attained only through Allah's grace and kindness.

Now observe the manners of life of Sulayman (peace be upon him). He too is in such circumstances that in the twinkling of an eye the throne of the Queen of Sheba is before him. See how the Qur'an records his states in such circumstances of strength and dignity.

﴿Falamma ra'ahu ... karim﴾ (27:40) "When he saw it placed beside him, he said: This is by the grace of my Lord, to test me whether I give thanks or am ungrateful. Whoever gives thanks, gives thanks for his own benefit; and whoever is ungrateful, indeed my Lord is Free of need, Generous."

And this was the way of Muhammad ﷺ. He adopted this manner throughout his whole life, and at the occasion of help and victory, which Allah had made a special sign for him, the Messenger was bowed down upon his riding animal. He entered Makkah in this same manner, with his head bowed. Today he entered that Makkah which had given him torments, which had expelled him from his home, which had fought him continuously, and which had stubbornly stood in opposition to his call. When help and victory were granted to him, he did not sound the drums of triumph and joy. He was bowing down, giving thanks to his Lord, occupied in praise, and as his Lord had instructed him, he was glorifying, declaring Allah's oneness, and seeking forgiveness. As it is reported in the narrations, after him his companions also maintained this same attitude. May Allah be pleased with them.

Thus humanity was raised high through faith. The face of humanity became radiant. It became pure and clear. Now humanity has reached the lofty station of greatness, strength and freedom.
